summary: Transactional prefill cursors, latency chunk policy, independent physical batch/workspace limits and borrowed-progress staging
implementation_scope: Adapter-side pending/committed chunk cursor with optional short-tail folding, immutable token staging and bounded exact-word repeated-passage observation over accepted reasoning; scheduling, model state and recovery/stop policy remain external; C++20 monotonic shape-cost chunk selector with fixed/linear/attention-pair/decode costs, hard bounds and fixed fallback; portable ordered physical batch plans with explicit atomic/padding rules, per-shape workspace bounds and an owned synchronous host scratch executor

agent_guidance.use_when: Expose bounded prompt work and preserve borrowed output tokens through model commit
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Existing engine/session helpers already meet the core handoff; this is not a scheduler replacement
provides: Bounded next chunk with commit/rollback cursor
Short-tail folding: a remainder of at most fold_limit tokens joins the previous chunk, and chunk_plan gives the lengths
Wait, copy, output-bound validation and logical token-byte reservation
Owned token snapshot plus its reservation owner
Streaming Unicode word accumulation and exact repeated-passage union coverage with bounded history
Largest feasible prefill chunk under a calibrated latency estimate, with occupied context, co-batched decode cost, alignment, workspace and quota bounds
Independent inherited/overridden physical column caps, safe atomic splitting, padded-shape byte planning and fixed-size host scratch reuse
engine_supplies: Model work and transactional state coordinated with the cursor at valid completed chunk boundaries
Successful readiness and physical resource reservations
Core scheduling, commit/publication and reservation lifetime
Accepted reasoning-channel text, workload-calibrated observation cadence/thresholds and explicit compatible stop or recovery policy
Legal splitting/padding declaration, exact workspace layout sizing, private state rollback and settled backend allocation/reservations
preserve: Pending work never advances the committed cursor early
Admitted output limit and owned-storage lifetime
A folded chunk exceeds the chunk limit by at most the fold limit; buffers are sized for that
Physical tiling preserves logical work and ordered state; scratch cannot be reused until each call settles; no automatic split of whole-block operations
adapt: Chunk size and prefill/decode policy priced by inter-token latency, prompt time and throughput
Cursor implementation integrated into engine state
Fold limit priced by the cost of re-reading the weights for a short chunk
Separate target/draft physical caps selected by measured complete-round cost and memory at fixed context and logical draft width

code_files.purpose: Adapter-side pending/committed chunk cursor and immutable token staging; scheduling and model-state transitions remain external
Bounded streaming Unicode word history and exact repeated-passage coverage; observation only, without model mutation or automatic stopping
Hardware/model-neutral latency chunk policy with explicit cost coefficients, exhaustive-oracle native tests and safe fallback
Portable physical caps, ordered atomic/padded shapes, exact per-shape scratch planning and synchronous owned host workspace

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library for host cursors; C++20 standard library for native policies and host scratch; backend hardware is an engine choice
requires.model: Engine exposes incremental prompt work and generated token candidates
requires.workload: Bounded work opportunities and signed 32-bit token staging with declared output limits

contract.input: Prompt, chunk/output budgets, borrowed tokens and readiness; physical cap, explicit split/padding rules, logical column extent and exact shape-to-workspace sizing
contract.output: Committed prefill cursor and owned StagedProgress; ordered physical shapes and peak scratch bytes
contract.ownership: Consumer owns model cursor/state. Core owns work selection, reservation lifetime, commit/publication and retirement.
contract.failure: Reject double advance, missing commit, invalid work budgets, token representation overflow and excess output. Physical plans reject illegal splits, overflow and over-budget workspaces before execution; callback failure/cancellation stops calls but engine state rollback remains external.
contract.core_boundary: Map next_chunk and staged progress to Session.advance/commit; return borrowed progress only under its lifetime contract.

dependencies: C++20 standard library for native policies and host scratch execution

validation.host: Host fixtures and worked example cover chunk rollback, empty prompt, staging order and token-byte accounting; repetition fixtures cover Unicode fragment equivalence, warmup, overlap union, bounded aging, unique text and atomic word-overflow failure
validation.native: Native chunk policy checked against 6000 exhaustive feasible searches, linear/context-dependent models and malformed calibration; Core integration tests enforce advice/grant bounds. No device or model qualification. Physical batches: 5000 shape-oracle cases, atomic/padded boundaries, independent caps, nonlinear workspace sizing, overflow, empty work, real scratch allocation/reuse and cancellation/failure/concurrent-use rejection.
validation.performance: Unmeasured for a native engine; host fixture success is not a speed claim
